title: Fuzzy-Bridge Delta Validator and Slowpath Reconciler for Usage Ingest
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: the current usage-event intake is brittle when clients send fields with minor typing drift (e.g., stringified numbers, optional nested maps with changed keys), and we lack a safe slowpath for events that need reconciliation or backfill after schema negotiation. This causes errors bubbled to callers and spikes in rejections during SDK upgrades and third-party integrations.

Goal: implement a 'Fuzzy-Bridge' ingestion layer that performs low-cost, deterministic normalization and a Delta Validator that grades how far an incoming event diverges from the canonical schema. Events with small, explainable deltas are auto-normalized; larger or ambiguous deltas are routed to a Slowpath Reconciler that stores the original, annotates diffs, and runs controlled automated repairs + human review flows. The system should preserve auditability and enable safe canary rewrites that replace old events with normalized versions for downstream consumers.

Scope:
- Build a lightweight normalization library (Go) with pluggable transformers (coercions: numeric<->string, timestamp backfills, key aliases).
- Implement a Delta Validator that computes a concise divergence score and structured delta tokens used for routing decisions.
- Add a Slowpath Reconciler service (separate worker pool) to accept high-divergence events and run staged reconciliation (autofix attempts, enqueue human triage, emit repair PR events).
- Provide metrics, dashboards, and alerting for delta rates, slowpath queue length, and reconciliation success rate.
- Design a staged rollout: shadow normalization -> canary rewrite for 1% of traffic -> 10% -> full.

Non-goals: not implementing a full type-inference engine; not changing downstream contract semantics without explicit rollout/consent.

Rationale and trade-offs:
- Conservative by default: prefer accepting and normalizing minor drifts rather than rejecting, to reduce customer visible errors.
- Keep normalization rules explicit and version-controlled to maintain reproducibility; avoid ad-hoc ML-based repair in first phase.
- Slowpath gives safety for ambiguous cases; it incurs storage and human review cost but avoids silent data corruption.

Architecture notes:
- Ingress HTTP LB -> Admission filter -> Fuzzy-Bridge transformer -> Delta Validator -> Router: Fastpath (normalized, validated) or Slowpath (persisted with raw payload + delta tokens) -> Downstream fanout.
- Use existing event-store (S3-backed revisioned bucket) for slowpath artifacts and a Redis-backed queue for worker coordination.
- Delta tokens are compact strings (e.g., T:+alias[user_id];F:-field_x;C:coerce:int_from_str) to keep routing decisions lightweight.

Acceptance criteria (must be met before full rollout):
- Fuzzy-Bridge reduces explicit ingestion rejections for SDK v2.3 by >= 75% in shadow mode.
- Delta Validator computes divergence score within 5ms P95 for 95% of events.
- Slowpath queue retention and processing pipeline processes 95% of enqueued events within 24 hours in canary.
- End-to-end observability: dashboard with delta histogram, top delta tokens, per-tenant slowpath rate.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for each transformer and coercion rule.
- Property-based tests for round-trip normalization (apply -> serialize -> validate).
- Synthetic fuzz harness (existing telemetry-fuzzer) to generate drift scenarios and assert safe classification.
- Canary traffic tests using a mix of real production replay (scrubbed) and mutation operators.

Rollout plan:
1) Deploy Fuzzy-Bridge in shadow mode for 100% traffic; collect deltas for 2 weeks.
2) Tune normalization rules and implement safe autofix list.
3) Canary rewrite: enable automatic normalized writes for 1% of eligible traffic and monitor consumer regressions.
4) Expand to 10% and then full if metrics stable and no critical regressions.

Observability and runbook:
- Dashboards: console/ingest/delta-rate, console/ingest/slowpath-latency, console/ingest/top-deltas.
- Alerts: slowpath queue > 500 items sustained for 10m (P0); delta-rate spike > 3x baseline (P1).
- Runbook actions: pause normalization, toggle canary flag per-tenant, engage oncall, open triage ticket linking slowpath artifacts.

Privacy/audit: Raw events persisted to slowpath store must follow retention and encryption policies (use KMS key ARN project-specific). All reconciliations must create immutable audit entries.

Deliverables:
- Go library: fuzzybridge v1.0 (pkg/fuzzybridge)
- Delta Validator service + API (POST /validate -> {score, tokens})
- Slowpath Reconciler worker that uses existing reconciliation UI for human review
- Dashboards and alerts in Datadog
- Confluence doc and migration guide

updates: 2025-10-01 - Kickoff: outlined approach with PM and infra; agreed to reuse Redis queue and S3-backed event-store. Action: define initial coercion rules.
2025-11-12 - Prototype: basic coercions implemented (numeric coerce, timestamp parse, alias map). Early tests show 40% rejection reduction with shadowing.

2025-12-05 - Design review: Security requested explicit KMS key usage for slowpath artifacts; added encryption requirement to design. Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFER/Fuzzy-Bridge+Design
2026-01-18 - Integration: Delta token format finalized to compact string tokens. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingest/pull/4123
2026-02-10 - Canary prep: prepared canary flagging by tenant; added Datadog dashboards. QA to run two-week synthetic replay.
2026-02-28 - In Review: implementation largely complete; seeking security review for S3 lifecycle policy and release approval from Console PM. Pending: human review UI wire-up and final DAG tuning.
notes: Follow-up: coordinate with SDK team for alias map for client-side upgrade guidance.
Consider later phase: ML-based clusterer to suggest normalization rules from slowpath corpus.
Keep normalization rules under feature-flagged config to allow fast rollback per-tenant.
